newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus agency suspends rating for 2 Pakistan banks.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus agency suspends rating for 2 Pakistan banks.

text.p: Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence has suspended long- and short-term ratings for Pakistan-based Habib Bank and United Bank until further notice, the specialist bank rating agency announced.
New ratings will be assigned once the banks' future has been resolved as regards their future privatisation, Capital Intelligence said on Friday.
Based on year-end 1995 total assets, Habib Bank Limited (HBL) and United Bank Limited (UBL) are the second and fourth largest commercial banks in Pakistan.
Both banks were brought under state control in 1974 with the passing of the Banks (nationalisation) Act, and became important instruments for implementing government monetary and banking policy.

Capital Intelligence said that under successive governments, undue political influence was exerted on the banks to extend credit in support of, inter alia, uneconomic enterprises and fatally flawed projects. The extent of the problem first surfaced in 1993 when the then caretaker government of Moeen Qureshi issued a list of loan defaulters.

Since then problem credits have continued to accumulate; it is estimated that non-performing loans represent over 30 percent of the respective banks' loan portfolios, and many times their respective capital bases. The banks' survival relies entirely on state support.
As a consequence, Capital Intelligence believes that HBL and UBL can be considered as bearing the same credit risk as the State of Pakistan.

Following the instalment of the current caretaker government under the leadership of Meraj Khalid, the privatisation of key state-owned banks has once again become a priority. As widely publicised, UBL and HBL are expected to be among the first institutions to be sold.
